items.stem: If f(x) = x², then f′(3) equals:
items.note: f′(x) = 2x → f′(3) = 6. The derivative gives the gradient of the tangent at that point.

items.stem: The derivative of 4x³ is:
items.note: Power rule: multiply by the power, reduce it by one. 4 × 3 = 12, power 3 → 2.

items.stem: The gradient of the tangent to y = x² at the point (3, 9) is:
items.note: dy/dx = 2x → at x = 3 the gradient is 6. The point's y-coordinate is irrelevant to the gradient.

items.stem: The equation of the tangent to y = x² at the point (3, 9) is:
items.note: Gradient 6 through (3, 9): y − 9 = 6(x − 3) → y = 6x − 9. Tangent questions need the point AND the gradient.

items.stem: The gradient of the NORMAL to the curve y = x² at the point (3, 9) is:
items.note: The normal is perpendicular to the tangent: gradient = −1/tangent gradient = −1/6.

items.stem: The function f(x) = x² − 6x + 5 has its minimum at x = 3. This is confirmed by the second derivative test because:
items.note: Stationary point: f′ = 0. f″ > 0 → minimum (concave up); f″ < 0 → maximum. f″ = 0 needs further investigation.

items.stem: The function f(x) = x³ − 3x is decreasing for:
items.note: f′(x) = 3x² − 3 < 0 → x² < 1 → −1 < x < 1. Solve f′ > 0 or < 0 by sign, then read the interval.

items.stem: The chain rule gives the derivative of (2x + 1)⁵ as:
items.note: Chain rule (linear inner): multiply by the inner derivative — 5 × 2 = 10. Forgetting the ×2 is the most common slip.

items.stem: The function f(x) = 2x³ − 9x² + 12x has stationary points at x = 1 and x = 2. Using the second derivative, x = 1 is:
items.note: f″(x) = 12x − 18: f″(1) = −6 < 0 → maximum at x = 1; f″(2) = 6 > 0 → minimum at x = 2.

items.stem: The value of the definite integral ∫₀² 3x² dx is:
items.note: Antiderivative: x³. Evaluate [x³]₀² = 8 − 0 = 8. Definite integrals have no +c.

items.stem: The indefinite integral of 3x² is:
items.note: ∫3x² dx = x³ + c — the constant of integration is required for every indefinite integral.

items.stem: The area enclosed by the curve y = 4 − x² and the x-axis is:
items.note: Roots at x = ±2: area = ∫₋₂² (4 − x²) dx = [4x − x³/3] = (16 − 16/3) − (−16 + 16/3) = 32/3 ≈ 10.7. Find the roots first to get the limits.

items.stem: A particle moves so that its velocity is v(t) = 3t² − 12t + 9 (t ≥ 0). The particle is at rest when:
items.note: At rest → v = 0: 3(t − 1)(t − 3) = 0 → t = 1, 3. Kinematics uses derivatives as rates of change.

items.stem: A particle moves with s(t) = t³ − 6t² + 9t. Its velocity at t = 2 is:
items.note: v = s′ = 3t² − 12t + 9 → v(2) = 12 − 24 + 9 = −3. The negative sign means moving in the negative direction.

items.stem: A rectangle has a perimeter of 20 m. Its maximum possible area is:
items.note: A = x(10 − x) = 10x − x²; A′ = 10 − 2x = 0 → x = 5 → 5 × 5 = 25 m². The maximum rectangle is always the square.

items.stem: For f(x) = 2x³ − 9x² + 12x, the local maximum value is:
items.note: Stationary points x = 1 and x = 2; f″(1) < 0 → maximum. The maximum VALUE is f(1) = 2 − 9 + 12 = 5 — quote the value, not just the x.

items.stem: A curve has dy/dx = 6x² − 4 and passes through the point (1, 3). Its equation is:
items.note: Integrate: y = 2x³ − 4x + c; substitute the point: 3 = 2 − 4 + c → c = 5. Every differential-equation answer needs c found from the given point.

items.stem: The area enclosed by y = 4 − x², the x-axis and the lines x = 0 and x = 2 is:
items.note: ∫₀² (4 − x²) dx = [4x − x³/3]₀² = 8 − 8/3 = 16/3. All values positive on [0, 2], so the integral IS the area here.

items.stem: An antiderivative of 6x² − 4 is:
items.note: Integrate term by term: 6x² → 2x³ (raise power, divide), −4 → −4x. Differentiate your answer to check.

items.stem: A ball is thrown so that its height is h(t) = 20t − 5t² (t in seconds, h in metres). It reaches its maximum height when:
items.note: h′ = 20 − 10t = 0 → t = 2; h(2) = 40 − 20 = 20 m; h″ = −10 < 0 → maximum. Optimisation questions ask for the VALUE too.

items.stem: A farmer has 40 m of fencing to build a rectangular pen against a straight river — no fencing is needed along the river. Find the dimensions of the pen that maximise its area, and state that area.
markscheme: Let x be the width (perpendicular to the river); the length is 40 − 2x (1)
items.tactic: Optimisation template: define variables → write the constraint → substitute into the objective → differentiate → solve → justify the maximum (second derivative) → answer the actual question asked.

items.stem: A particle moves in a straight line with displacement s(t) = t³ − 9t² + 24t metres for t ≥ 0. (a) Find the velocity function. (b) Find when the particle is at rest. (c) Find its acceleration at t = 3.
markscheme: (b) 3(t − 2)(t − 4) = 0 → at rest at t = 2 s and t = 4 s (1)
items.tactic: Kinematics chain: displacement → velocity (differentiate once) → acceleration (differentiate twice). 'At rest' means v = 0 — set the derivative to zero and solve.
